question: The unit panel's brigade_view and sunk_ships_view windows, with making a ship the pride of the fleet: what opens them, every row, and what is posted.

addresses.name: CBrigadeView::CBrigadeView
addresses.signature: CBrigadeView* __stdcall CBrigadeView::CBrigadeView(CSubUnit* brigade@ECX, CBrigadeView* storage@stack:4, CInGameIdler* screen@stack:8) @EAX
addresses.comment: **The constructor of `brigade_view`, RTTI class CBrigadeView** (0xBC bytes, vftable 0x15D626C, glue table 0x15D6280 - it was recorded as UnitStatsWindow_Construct, 'in no class with RTTI', which was wrong). Its three CButtonObserverGlue members: +0x4 `close` -> 0x327120 (closed flag +0x88), +0x30 `sunk` -> CBrigadeView::OnSunkClicked, +0x5C `make_pride` -> CBrigadeView::OnMakePrideClicked. Keeps the sub-unit (+0x8C pointer, +0x90/+0x94 its id pair) and the in-game screen (+0xB8), makes the window `brigade_view` (+0xB4). Fills once, at construction: `photo` through CInGameIdler::SetSubUnitPhoto (builder's tag, or the owner's where no builder); exactly one of unit_experience_land/air/naval shown (frame 1 under an experience of 1, else round(experience with pride / 10) + 2, at most 11, the other two hidden) by the definition's is_land, is_air, is_ship; `label` = '(' + yellow model name + '+*' where PickBestModel differs from FindModelOf + white ')' newline, or the definition's name where no model; `subunit_name` edit box = the sub-unit's name with '"' refused and read-only (edit +0x159 = 1) where a scenario is running; then the rows of `list`, each a CBrigadeStatsEntry: UNIT_STATS with an empty value; BV_STRENGTH, BV_EXPERIENCE, MAX_STRENGTH (land only), DEFAULT_ORG, DEFAULT_MORALE, RADIO_STRENGTH, MAXIMUM_SPEED, SUPPLY_CONSUMPTION, FUEL_CONSUMPTION; then the land, ship or air block (see the findings); a blank row; CBrigadeView_AddAdjusterRows for NIGHT, FORT, RIVER, AMPH and every terrain; a blank row; UNIT_MODELS and one row per technology on the sub-unit's list. Nothing here is refilled later: only CBrigadeView::Update touches the window again. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sunkships.md, section 3.
addresses.revises: Renamed from UnitStatsWindow_Construct and given a class: the two tables it writes are CBrigadeView's (RTTI vftable 0x15D626C, its glue 0x15D6280) and its old comment's 'in no class with RTTI' was wrong. The signature's return is now the window it returns.
addresses.evidence: findRefs --vftable CBrigadeView gives this function and CBrigadeView's destructor as the only two writers of 0x15D626C. Row order read from the decompilation (0x31F460) and the listing at 0x71F5D3.. against the keys' strings. Shown wrong if the vftable at 0x15D626C were not CBrigadeView's in the RTTI export.

addresses.name: CSubUnitEntry::OnClicked
addresses.comment: Slot 4: a plain click on the row's `select` button (its glue's slot 2, +0x8, the vcall stub 0x27A310). Nothing for the row of an upgrade in progress (+0x120). Otherwise resolves the sub-unit and, **unless the in-game screen's list of open cards (+0x20) already holds its id**, appends the id and opens a CBrigadeView (CBrigadeView::CBrigadeView, CEU3Idler::AddDialog). Any brigade, ship or wing of the panel's unit - the row asks nothing of its owner. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sunkships.md, section 2.
addresses.revises: The comment still named the constructor BuildUnitStatsTooltip; it is CBrigadeView::CBrigadeView now, and this says which click reaches it and what the +0x120 test and the screen's +0x20 list are. Name and signature unchanged.
addresses.evidence: The ctor at 0x748D90 binds glue +0x28 on the element at 0x749060 with the plain-click slot pointing at 0x67A310 (vcall slot 4, listing 0x748E6C) and the list id test reads the screen's +0x20 (decompilation of 0x749EE0).

addresses.name: CBrigadeView::~CBrigadeView
addresses.comment: **Where a rename happens**: if the window and the sub-unit still exist, the `subunit_name` edit box's text, whitespace trimmed; if it differs from the sub-unit's name, is not empty and no scenario is running, posts CRenameSubUnitCommand(sub-unit, text). Then drops the window (slot 20 of the type) and takes the sub-unit's id off the screen's list of open cards (+0x20). `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sunkships.md, section 3.3.
addresses.evidence: The listing at 0x726B88..0x726CE5 (slot 20 of the name element's text, 0x4173C0 String_Equals, 0x5DDD90 the 0x80-byte command, the queue's post) and the decompilation's ordering of the three guards. Shown wrong if the command at 0x5DDD90 were not CRenameSubUnitCommand; its vftable write at 0x5DDE0D is 0x15C8E9C, that class's table.

addresses.name: CBrigadeView::~CBrigadeView_scalar_deleting
addresses.comment: Slot 0, the deleting form: CBrigadeView::~CBrigadeView and free where bit 0 of flags is set. Named by RTTI in Ghidra already; recorded for the slot.
addresses.evidence: Slot 0 of the table at 0x15D626C holds it; the body is the call and the free, as for every scalar deleting destructor. Shown wrong if it were not slot 0 of the RTTI table.

addresses.name: CBrigadeView::Update
addresses.comment: Slot 1, every frame from the idler's dialog list; false means the idler deletes the window. Re-resolves the sub-unit; gone -> false. **Slot 10 of the sub-unit (true only for a CShip)**: false hides `make_pride` and `sunk` every frame. For a ship: `sunk` is enabled when some entry of g_CCurrentGameState->sunk_ships has that ship as its sunk_by (FindPersistentByIdPair of +0x9C/+0xA0 == this ship) and disabled when none does; `make_pride` is hidden where the definition's can_be_pride (+0x39) is clear, else disabled for a ship already pride (+0xA5) and enabled for one that is not. Returns the opposite of the closed flag (+0x88). Touches nothing else - the rows are built once. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sunkships.md, section 3.2.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly of 0x726D70..0x72711D (button slot 46/47 enable/disable and slot 14 hide, the sunk-list walk at 0x726E7E). CRegiment's slot 10 is 0x592360 (false), CShip's 0xA92590 (true), CWing's 0x592360 (false) off the RTTI tables. Would be wrong if the slot index or a table were misread.

addresses.name: CBrigadeView::OnSunkClicked
addresses.comment: `sunk`'s plain click (glue +0x30, handler at glue +8): resolves the sub-unit and hands a new 0x60-byte CSunkenShipsView to CEU3Idler::AddDialog. No test of whether one is open already, so each press opens another. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sunkships.md, section 3.4.
addresses.evidence: The decompilation of 0x727130 and its one reference, the glue member written at +0x38 of the constructor (0x71F4D6). Shown wrong if the +0x38 member were not the plain-click slot.

addresses.name: CBrigadeView::OnMakePrideClicked
addresses.comment: `make_pride`'s plain click: resolves the ship and hands a new 0x94-byte CConfirmMakePride to CEU3Idler::AddDialog. Nothing is changed until the dialog is confirmed; no test of an open dialog, so each press opens another. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sunkships.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation of 0x727270; the 0x94 allocation, the constructor call and AddDialog. Reference at +0x64 of the constructor (0x71F4FF).

addresses.name: CBrigadeView_AddAdjusterRows
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CBrigadeView_AddAdjusterRows(CBrigadeView* view, CInGameIdler* screen, Hoi3CString* name, CUnitAdjuster* adjuster)
addresses.comment: Up to four rows for one adjuster, each only if that field is not 0, in order: UA_ATTACK (+0x8), UA_DEFENCE (+0xC), UA_MOVEMENT (+0x10), UA_ATTRITION (+0x14). Label: `name` + ' ' + the key's text. Value: '+' where positive, then the figure: the first three times 100 to 2 places, **attrition as it stands to 2 places, not times 100**, then '%'. `ret 0x10`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sunkships.md, section 3.5.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation of 0x7259D0 and the listing of the fourth arm at 0x7266E2..0x726783 (no call of the x100/x1000 helpers, FormatFixedPoint directly on +0x14). Shown wrong if the first three arms lacked the multiply.

addresses.name: CBrigadeStatsEntry::CBrigadeStatsEntry
addresses.signature: CBrigadeStatsEntry* __thiscall CBrigadeStatsEntry::CBrigadeStatsEntry(CInGameIdler* screen, CBrigadeStatsEntry* storage, Hoi3CString label, Hoi3CString value)

addresses.evidence: Decompilation of 0x31E650: the two text elements by name and SetText on the two by-value strings (stack +8 and +0x24), and its RTTI record introduces no slot. The ret 0x3C is 4 + 0x1C + 0x1C.

addresses.name: CSunkenShipsView::CSunkenShipsView
addresses.signature: CSunkenShipsView* __stdcall CSunkenShipsView::CSunkenShipsView(CSunkenShipsView* storage, CSubUnit* ship, CInGameIdler* screen)
addresses.comment: The window `sunk_ships_view`: the sub-unit (+0x34, id pair +0x38/+0x3C) and the window (+0x5C); the `close` glue (+0x4) -> CSunkenShipsView::OnClose. A CSunkenShipEntry for each ship on g_CCurrentGameState->sunk_ships whose sunk_by (+0x9C/+0xA0) resolves to this sub-unit, in list order; `label` = SUNK_SHIP_LABEL with NAME the sub-unit's name; the window shown. `ret 0xC`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sunkships.md, section 5.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation of 0x31E100 (walk of the list at state +0x20, FindPersistentByIdPair == the ship, `list`, SUNK_SHIP_LABEL), one caller CBrigadeView::OnSunkClicked. Shown wrong if the comparison were to the sunk ship rather than its sinker.

addresses.name: CSunkenShipsView::~CSunkenShipsView
addresses.comment: Slot 0, the deleting destructor: drops the window through its slot 20 (+0x50), frees the sub-unit id's cached name and resets the observer. Named by RTTI in Ghidra; recorded for the slot.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation; slot 0 of table 0x15D622C.

addresses.name: CSunkenShipsView::Update
addresses.comment: Slot 1, every frame: re-resolves the sub-unit (gone: false, and the idler deletes the window); otherwise answers the opposite of the closed flag (+0x30). Nothing is refilled, so the list is what was on the sunk list when the window opened.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation of 0x31E5E0; slot 1 of 0x15D622C.

addresses.name: CSunkenShipsView::OnClose
addresses.comment: The `close` button's plain click (+0x30 = 1). The only thing the window's buttons do; not in the class's tables, reached through the glue at +0x4.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly: `mov byte ptr [ecx+0x30], 1; ret`, the glue's +0xC of the constructor (0x71E12F region) points at it.

addresses.name: CSunkenShipEntry::CSunkenShipEntry
addresses.signature: CSunkenShipEntry* __stdcall CSunkenShipEntry::CSunkenShipEntry(CSunkenShipEntry* storage, CInGameIdler* screen, CSubUnit* ship)
addresses.comment: A row of `sunk_ships_view`'s `list`: window `sunk_ship` into +0x20. `name` = the ship's name (slot 8); `counter_type` = sprite GFX_counter_ + the type's key where that sprite exists (slot 57); `country` = the owner's flag (slot 53, CSubUnit +0x98); `model` = the historical model's name (CHistoricalModel::PickBestModel, of the builder's country, the owner's where there is no builder) + '+*' where it is not FindModelOf's, or the definition's own name where the type has no model. Inherits every slot of the list item: **a row has no tooltip and a click does nothing**. `ret 0xC`.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation; RTTI gives the class no introduced slot, and the only slot that differs from CStandardlistboxItem is the folded destructor at 0x31E820.

addresses.name: CConfirmMakePride::CConfirmMakePride
addresses.signature: CConfirmMakePride* __thiscall CConfirmMakePride::CConfirmMakePride(CInGameIdler* screen, CConfirmMakePride* storage, CSubUnit* ship)
addresses.comment: The `DefaultConfirm` dialog of `make_pride` (0x94 bytes): the screen at +0x68, the ship by id at +0x6C/+0x70/+0x74. Title CONFIRM_MAKE_PRIDE_TITLE; description CONFIRM_MAKE_PRIDE_DESC with EFFECTS = MAKE_PRIDE_EXP_EFFECT (NAME the ship, EXP PRIDE_BONUS_EXP to 0 places) + MAKE_PRIDE_SUNK_EFFECT (NAME) + where the owner already has a pride (CCountry_FindPrideOfTheFleet, by CSubUnit +0x94): MAKE_PRIDE_PREVIOUS_EFFECT (OLD_NAME that ship) and, where GetPrideRedesignationDissent is above 0, MAKE_PRIDE_DISSENT_EFFECT (DISSENT, 2 places). `ret 8`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sunkships.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation of 0x31E8A0 and the listing at 0x71ECED (owner tag read for FindPride). One caller CBrigadeView::OnMakePrideClicked.

addresses.name: CConfirmMakePride::OnConfirm
addresses.comment: Slot 5, Ok: makes a 0x64-byte CMakePrideCommand with the ship (id pair +0x70/+0x74 resolved) and posts it through the session's queue; sets the dialog's +0x64 (closed); sets the screen's reshow_open_view (+0xD30) unless a custom game's setting +0x18 is 2.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation of 0x31F2A0; the post is the one written out in CConfirmRemoveAll::OnConfirm's record.

addresses.name: CConfirmMakePride::StaysOpen
addresses.comment: Slot 7: whether the ship still resolves; false shuts the dialog with no effect. The dialog's closed flag is CEU3Dialog::Update's business.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation of 0x31F400. Shape identical to CConfirmDisbandAll::StaysOpen.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::SetSubUnitPhoto
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CInGameIdler::SetSubUnitPhoto(CInGameIdler* this, void* icon, CCountryTag country, CSubUnit* subUnit)
addresses.comment: Slot 77: puts the model picture of a sub-unit on an icon. Path `<gfx folder>/models/` (the gfx folder's mode: an override directory with the base or both), type = the sub-unit's definition's key: default `<type>_0.tga`; where PickBestModel gives model N of the country's set: `<TAG>_<type>_N.tga` if that file exists, else `<type>_N.tga` if that exists, else the default; where there is no model the code tries `<TAG>_<type>_0.tga` **but without the /models/ prefix**, so it is never found (the original's slip). If the chosen file exists, it is made a texture on `GFX_no_ship_selected`'s footprint and set on the icon (slot 56) and the icon shown (slot 13); if not, the icon keeps what the file gives it.
addresses.evidence: Listing of 0x677410.. : the strings '/models/', '_0.tga', '.tga', '_', the three FileExists arms and the missing '/models/' at 0x677CD0.. in the no-model arm. Slot 77 of table 0x15CEB54, one holder (vtable.py --holding).

addresses.name: CMakePrideCommand::CMakePrideCommand
addresses.comment: Makes the 0x64-byte command naming a ship (the id pair at +0x40/+0x44 Execute resolves). `ret 8`. Posted only by CConfirmMakePride::OnConfirm.
addresses.evidence: Its call from CConfirmMakePride::OnConfirm with the 0x64-byte allocation; ret 8; the id pair is what CMakePrideCommand::Execute reads.
